program: csv shipments.csv where region eq north each units map [ if [ ge 12 ] [ "heavy" ] [ if [ ge 4 ] [ "medium" ] [ "light" ] ] ] freq sort 0 map [ fmt "{0} - {1}" ] print

task: Write a Ken program that reads `shipments.csv` and works out the number of distinct clients for each region, considering only shipments with result other than `returned` and from the month `2026-04`, and then prints all results from the largest value to the smallest, in the format `region: distinct`.
program: csv shipments.csv where result ne returned where sent has 2026-04 by region [ each client nuniq ] pairs rsort 1 map [ fmt "{0}: {1}" ] print

task: Write a Ken program that classifies every one of the orders by its `price`: `bottom` if it is less than 50, `middle` if it is less than 289, and `top` otherwise. Print the number of orders in each class, most numerous first, in the format `class: count`.
program:
def kind [ if [ lt 50 ] [ "bottom" ] [ if [ lt 289 ] [ "middle" ] [ "top" ] ] ]
csv orders.csv as o
o each price map [ kind ] freq map [ fmt "{0}: {1}" ] print

program: csv bookings.csv where guest in elena,ines where city eq paris by room [ each nights mean round 2 ] pairs sort 1 first 2 map [ fmt "{0}: {1}" ] print

task: Write a Ken program that computes the ratio of the number of distinct items to the total number of units (`units`) for every month, considering only shipments with item `pallet`, rounded to 2 decimal places, then displays the 4 entries with the largest value (descending), one per line in the format `month - ratio`.
program: csv shipments.csv where item eq pallet set month [ sent slice 0 7 ] by month [ as g g each item nuniq as a g each units sum as y a div y round 2 ] top 4 map [ fmt "{0} - {1}" ] print

task: Write a Ken program that determines the lowest guest rating (`rating`) among bookings where `rating` is at least 3 and prints just the value.
program: csv bookings.csv where rating ge 3 each rating min print

task: Write a Ken program that computes, for each item, its share of the total cost (`units` × `unit_cost`) among shipments where `unit_cost` is less than 50, as a percentage rounded to 1 decimal place, and then prints the 2 entries with the largest value (descending), one per line in the format `item: X%`.
program: csv shipments.csv where unit_cost lt 50 set rev [ units mul unit_cost ] as full full each rev sum as total full by item [ each rev sum div total mul 100 round 1 ] top 2 map [ fmt "{0}: {1}%" ] print

task: Write a Ken program that works out the total cost (`units` × `unit_cost`) for each month, and then outputs all results from the largest value to the smallest, in the format `month; cost` (first print the text `Summary:`).
program: "Summary:" print csv shipments.csv set rev [ units mul unit_cost ] set month [ sent slice 0 7 ] group month map [ each rev sum round 2 ] pairs rsort 1 map [ fmt "{0}; {1}" ] print

task: Write a Ken program that reads `orders.csv` and calculates the largest single order value (`qty` × `price`) among orders with product `headphones` and with category `electronics` and prints just the value (first print the text `Summary:`).
program: "Summary:" print csv orders.csv where product eq headphones where category eq electronics set rev [ qty mul price ] each rev max round 2 print

task: Write a Ken program that for each product category computes the number of distinct products, and then displays alphabetically only the entries whose value is at least 3, in the format `category; distinct` (first print the text `Data:`).
program: "Data:" print csv orders.csv group category map [ each product nuniq ] pairs filter [ get 1 ge 3 ] sort 0 map [ fmt "{0}; {1}" ] print
